docs.title: rodeo
docs.text: rodeo receives push events from GitHub and GitLab, checks that each one really came from your provider, and then acts on it. It can run hooks inside the service, or run the commands listed in a rodeo.toml file in your repository. That file is how you deploy on push.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text:
1. Install rodeo with Docker, or on Linux and macOS or Windows.
  2. Configure the two webhook secrets.
  3. Run the service and connect your repositories.
  4. Deploy with rodeo.toml to run commands on every push.

docs.title: Requirements at a glance
docs.text:
Requirement Needed for Java 21 or newer Running rodeo outside Docker Git Cloning repositories for rodeo.toml commands sh on the PATH Running rodeo.toml commands (Git Bash on Windows) A public HTTPS address Receiving webhooks from GitHub or GitLab

Commands run on your server

Every command in a rodeo.toml runs on the machine that runs rodeo, with that machine's permissions. Anyone who can push to a listed repository controls what runs. Only enable repositories you trust. See rodeo.toml.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: rodeo is configured with environment variables. There is no configuration file to edit.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
Variable Required Default Description GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET Yes none Secret shared with the GitHub webhook. Used to verify the X-Hub-Signature-256 signature. GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET Yes none Secret token shared with the GitLab webhook. Sent in X-Gitlab-Token. PORT No 8080 Port the HTTP server listens on.

rodeo will not start unless both secrets are set. If one is missing, the log shows:

GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET must be set; refusing to accept unauthenticated webhooks

docs.title: Choosing secrets
docs.text:
Use a random value of at least 32 bytes. Generate one with:

openssl rand -hex 32

Use a different value for each provider. Enter the same value in the matching webhook settings. See Running rodeo.

docs.title: Setting the variables
docs.text:
Where rodeo runs How to set them Docker --env-file rodeo.env, see Docker Linux or macOS service EnvironmentFile= in the systemd unit, see Linux and macOS Windows Machine-level variables, see Windows Terminal, for testing export GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET=... (Bash) or $env:GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET = "..." (PowerShell)

Changing a secret

rodeo reads the secrets at startup. After you change one, restart rodeo and update the matching webhook in your provider. Deliveries sent in between are rejected with 401.

docs.title: Deploy on push
docs.text: This walkthrough deploys a Spring Boot application to a Linux server every time someone pushes to main. It uses rodeo and a rodeo.toml in the application's repository.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
git push origin main
      │
      ▼
GitHub or GitLab  ──webhook──▶  rodeo (on your server)
                                  │
                                  ├─ clones main into a temp directory
                                  ├─ reads rodeo.toml
                                  └─ runs ./scripts/deploy.sh
                                        │
                                        ├─ builds the jar
                                        ├─ copies it to /opt/app
                                        └─ restarts the app service

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• rodeo is installed and running, and reachable over HTTPS. See Install and Running rodeo.
  • The application's repository is public, because rodeo cannot clone private repositories yet.
  • The server has the tools the deploy needs: here, Maven and Java 21.
  • An application service named app already runs from /opt/app/app.jar, under systemd.

docs.title: 1. Add the rodeo.toml file
docs.text:
In the application's repository, create rodeo.toml at the root:

branches = ["main"]

commands = [
  "./scripts/deploy.sh",
]

Pushes to any other branch are ignored.

docs.title: 2. Add the deploy script
docs.text:
Create scripts/deploy.sh and make it executable (chmod +x scripts/deploy.sh):

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

mvn -B -q package -DskipTests

if [ -f /opt/app/app.jar ]; then
    cp /opt/app/app.jar /opt/app/app.jar.previous
fi
install -m 644 target/app-*.jar /opt/app/app.jar
sudo systemctl restart app

set -eu stops the script at the first error, so a failed build never replaces the running jar. The previous jar is kept as app.jar.previous for rollback.

docs.title: 3. Let rodeo restart the service
docs.text:
The rodeo user needs permission to restart only this service. Create /etc/sudoers.d/rodeo-app:

rodeo ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /bin/systemctl restart app

Check the file before you save it:

sudo visudo -cf /etc/sudoers.d/rodeo-app

The script must also be able to write /opt/app/app.jar, so give the rodeo user write access to that directory:

sudo chown rodeo /opt/app

docs.title: 4. Connect the repository
docs.text: Add the repository's webhook as described in Running rodeo. For GitHub, the payload URL is https://<your-host>/webhooks/github, and the event is Just the push event.

docs.title: 5. Deploy
docs.text:
Push a commit to main:

git commit --allow-empty -m "Trigger deploy"
git push origin main

Watch the run on the server:

journalctl -u rodeo -f

You should see lines like these, in order:

GITHUB push to acme/app on branch main by alice: 1 commit(s), head 9f8e7d6
Running './scripts/deploy.sh' in /tmp/rodeo-1234567890
Finished commands for acme/app on branch main

Confirm the application restarted:

systemctl status app

docs.title: Rolling back
docs.text:
Restore the jar the previous deploy saved, and restart the service:

sudo install -m 644 /opt/app/app.jar.previous /opt/app/app.jar
sudo systemctl restart app

The restore keeps only one previous version. Rolling back twice in a row requires a deploy of an older commit.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause The push shows 202 but no run appears in the log The branch is not listed in rodeo.toml, or the file is missing. See rodeo.toml logs. git clone failed The repository is private, or the branch name is wrong. Command exited with 1 The build failed. Read the output above that line. sudo: a password is required The sudoers rule is missing or has a different path to systemctl. Check which systemctl. The run takes longer than 10 minutes and is killed The build or deploy step is too slow for one command. Split the work into smaller commands, or run long jobs outside rodeo.

docs.title: Limits of this setup
docs.text: Deploy commands run directly on the server, outside any container. Anyone with push access to main can change what runs. Restrict who can push to main, and review changes to rodeo.toml and scripts/ the way you review production code.

docs.title: rodeo.toml
docs.text: A repository adds a file named rodeo.toml at its root to tell rodeo which commands to run on each push. rodeo reads the file from the pushed branch, so changing the file takes effect on the next push to that branch.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
branches = ["main"]

commands = [
  "mvn -B test",
  "./scripts/deploy.sh",
]
Key Type Required Description branches array of strings Yes Branches that trigger the commands. If the list is missing or empty, nothing runs. commands array of strings Yes Shell commands to run in order, from the root of the repository.

The file must be valid TOML. A syntax error stops the run and is written to the log.

docs.title: What happens on a push
docs.text:
1. rodeo receives a verified push event.
  2. Tag pushes are ignored.
  3. rodeo clones the branch into a new temporary directory with git clone --depth 1 --branch <branch>.
  4. If rodeo.toml is missing, or the branch is not listed in it, rodeo logs the reason and stops.
  5. Each command runs in order with sh -c, in the clone's root directory.
  6. The first command that fails stops the run. The remaining commands do not run.
  7. The temporary directory is deleted, whatever the outcome.

Pushes are processed one at a time, in the order they arrive. A slow run delays the runs queued behind it.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Limit Value Clone time 5 minutes Time per command 10 minutes. A command still running after that is killed. Environment Only PATH and HOME are passed through. Other variables, including the webhook secrets, are not visible to commands. Repositories Public repositories. A private repository cannot be cloned, because rodeo sends no credentials. Output Written to rodeo's standard output. Redirect it to a file if you need to keep it.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
rodeo logs each step. The messages you will see most often:

Message Meaning Running '<command>' in <directory> A command is starting. No rodeo.toml in <repo>; nothing to run The clone has no rodeo.toml at its root. Branch <name> is not listed in rodeo.toml for <repo> The push was to a branch that is not in branches. Command exited with <code>: <command> A command failed, and the remaining commands were skipped. Command timed out after ... A command was killed for running too long. Commands failed for <repo> on branch <name> The clone or the file failed. The log entry includes the cause.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Commands run on the machine that runs rodeo, with that machine's permissions. Anyone who can push to a listed branch controls what runs on the server. Only enable repositories whose contributors you trust with that access.

Keep server secrets out of reach of the commands you run. The webhook secrets are not passed to commands, but anything else the service user can read is.

docs.title: Requirements on the server
docs.text:
• git on the PATH.
  • sh on the PATH. On Windows, use Git Bash, see Windows.
  • Every tool your commands call, such as mvn, node, or docker, installed on the server and on the PATH of the rodeo service.

Docker users: the image contains only git and sh. Add the tools you need, see Docker.

For an end-to-end example, see Deploy on push.

docs.title: Start
docs.text:
With rodeo installed and configured, start it using the method you chose:

Method Command Docker docker start rodeo systemd sudo systemctl start rodeo Windows java -jar rodeo-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar

When it is running, the log shows the port it listens on. Stop it with docker stop rodeo, sudo systemctl stop rodeo, or Ctrl+C in the terminal.

docs.title: Expose it over HTTPS
docs.text:
GitHub and GitLab send webhooks to a public HTTPS URL. Put rodeo behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS. With Caddy, this is enough:

rodeo.example.com {
    reverse_proxy localhost:8080
}

Caddy obtains the certificate automatically. With nginx, use proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080; inside a location / block and a certificate from your provider.

rodeo does not need to be reachable on any other path. Only /webhooks/github and /webhooks/gitlab accept requests. Everything else returns 403.

docs.title: Connect a repository
docs.text: Connect each repository to the matching endpoint. The payload URL is https://<your-host>/webhooks/github for GitHub and https://<your-host>/webhooks/gitlab for GitLab.

docs.title: GitHub
docs.text:
1. Open the repository, then go to Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook.
  2. Payload URL: https://<your-host>/webhooks/github
  3. Content type: application/json
  4. Secret: the value of GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET
  5. Which events: Just the push event
  6. Save.

To connect every repository in an organization, add the webhook at the organization level instead.

docs.title: GitLab
docs.text:
1. Open the project, then go to Settings → Webhooks → Add new webhook.
  2. URL: https://<your-host>/webhooks/gitlab
  3. Secret token: the value of GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET
  4. Trigger: Push events
  5. Save, then select Test → Push events to send a test delivery.

docs.title: Check that deliveries arrive
docs.text:
Push a commit, or use Recent Deliveries (GitHub) or Test (GitLab). A correctly signed push returns 202 Accepted.

rodeo logs one line per accepted push:

GITHUB push to octo/hello on branch main by octocat: 3 commit(s), head 1a2b3c4

You can test without a provider by sending a signed request yourself:

BODY='{"ref":"refs/heads/main","after":"abc","repository":{"full_name":"octo/hello"},"commits":[]}'
SIG="sha256=$(printf '%s' "$BODY" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET" | sed 's/^.* //')"

curl -i -X POST https://rodeo.example.com/webhooks/github \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-GitHub-Event: push' \
  -H "X-Hub-Signature-256: $SIG" \
  --data "$BODY"

docs.title: HTTP responses
docs.text: Request Status Meaning Push with a valid signature or token 202 Accepted. Hooks and any rodeo.toml commands are triggered. Other event, such as an issue or a tag push 202 Accepted and ignored. GitHub ping with a valid signature 200 rodeo is reachable. Missing or wrong signature or token 401 Rejected. Nothing ran. Any other path 403 Not served.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check Every delivery returns 401 The secret in rodeo and the secret in the provider are different. Re-enter the value in the provider. rodeo does not start One of the two secrets is not set. See Configuration. Deliveries return 202 but nothing runs The repository has no rodeo.toml, or the branch is not listed in it. See rodeo.toml. Connection refused or timeout from the provider The proxy is not reachable from the internet, or DNS does not point at the host.

docs.title: Install with Docker
docs.text: The image includes the rodeo service, Java 21, and Git. Build it from the project root.

docs.title: Build the image
docs.text: docker build -t rodeo:latest .

docs.title: Run the container
docs.text:
Pass the secrets with an environment file so they do not appear in your shell history:

cat > rodeo.env <<'EOF'
GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET=replace-with-a-long-random-string
GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET=replace-with-another-long-random-string
EOF
chmod 600 rodeo.env

docker run -d --name rodeo \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --env-file rodeo.env \
  -p 8080:8080 \
  rodeo:latest

Check that it started:

docker logs -f rodeo

docs.title: Commands in rodeo.toml
docs.text:
The image contains only git and sh. A rodeo.toml command that needs another tool, such as Maven, Node, or Docker, fails unless that tool is in the image. Build your own image on top of rodeo:latest and install what your commands need:

FROM rodeo:latest
USER root
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends maven \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
USER rodeo

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
Rebuild the image and replace the container. The secrets stay in rodeo.env:

docker build -t rodeo:latest .
docker rm -f rodeo
docker run -d --name rodeo --restart unless-stopped --env-file rodeo.env -p 8080:8080 rodeo:latest

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: Continue with Configuration and Running rodeo.

docs.title: Install on Linux and macOS
docs.text: These steps install rodeo directly on the host, without Docker.

docs.title: 1. Install the prerequisites
docs.text:
Debian and UbuntuFedora and RHELArch LinuxmacOS 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y openjdk-21-jdk-headless maven git

sudo dnf install -y java-21-openjdk-devel maven git

sudo pacman -S --needed jdk21-openjdk maven git

brew install openjdk@21 maven git
export JAVA_HOME="$(brew --prefix openjdk@21)/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home"
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"

Add the two export lines to your shell profile to keep them.

Confirm the versions:

java -version    # 21 or newer
mvn -version
git --version

docs.title: 2. Build the jar
docs.text:
From the project root:

mvn -B package

The jar is written to target/rodeo-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar. Copy it to a location for the service:

sudo mkdir -p /opt/rodeo
sudo cp target/rodeo-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar /opt/rodeo/rodeo.jar

docs.title: 3. Create a service user
docs.text:
Run rodeo as its own account, not as your login user:

sudo useradd --system --create-home --home-dir /var/lib/rodeo --shell /usr/sbin/nologin rodeo

docs.title: 4. Store the secrets
docs.text:
sudo mkdir -p /etc/rodeo
sudo tee /etc/rodeo/rodeo.env >/dev/null <<'EOF'
GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET=replace-with-a-long-random-string
GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET=replace-with-another-long-random-string
PORT=8080
EOF
sudo chown root:rodeo /etc/rodeo/rodeo.env
sudo chmod 640 /etc/rodeo/rodeo.env

docs.title: 5. Run as a service (systemd)
docs.text:
Create /etc/systemd/system/rodeo.service:

[Unit]
Description=rodeo webhook service
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
User=rodeo
EnvironmentFile=/etc/rodeo/rodeo.env
ExecStart=/usr/bin/java -jar /opt/rodeo/rodeo.jar
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

On macOS, run the jar directly, or write a launchd property list that sets the same variables.

Start the service:

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now rodeo
sudo systemctl status rodeo
journalctl -u rodeo -f

docs.title: Commands in rodeo.toml
docs.text: Commands run as the rodeo user, with PATH and HOME set from that user's environment. Install every tool your commands need system-wide, for example sudo apt-get install maven, so it is on the default PATH.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: Continue with Configuration and Running rodeo.

docs.title: Install on Windows
docs.text: These steps install rodeo directly on Windows, without Docker. Run the commands in PowerShell.

docs.title: 1. Install the prerequisites
docs.text:
Install the tools with winget:

winget install --id EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.21.JDK -e
winget install --id Apache.Maven -e
winget install --id Git.Git -e

Open a new PowerShell window so the new PATH entries load, then confirm:

java -version
mvn -version
git --version

Git Bash provides sh

rodeo runs rodeo.toml commands with sh. Git for Windows includes sh in its bin folder, which is not on PATH by default. Add it:

[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(
    "Path",
    [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "Machine") + ";C:\Program Files\Git\bin",
    "Machine")

Open a new PowerShell window afterwards and check with sh -c "echo ok".

docs.title: 2. Build the jar
docs.text:
From the project root:

mvn -B package

The jar is written to target\rodeo-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar.

docs.title: 3. Set the secrets
docs.text:
Set the variables for the machine, so they persist across restarts:

[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET", "replace-with-a-long-random-string", "Machine")
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET", "replace-with-another-long-random-string", "Machine")

Open a new PowerShell window before you run rodeo, so it picks them up.

docs.title: 4. Run
docs.text:
java -jar target\rodeo-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar

To run it in the background at startup, register it as a Windows service with a wrapper such as NSSM, pointing the service at java with the arguments -jar C:\rodeo\rodeo-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar. The service must run under an account that has the Machine variables and can reach your repositories.

docs.title: Commands in rodeo.toml
docs.text: Commands run through sh, so they use POSIX shell syntax such as &&, > and ./script.sh. Tools such as mvn must be on the system PATH. PowerShell scripts run as pwsh -File deploy.ps1 if you call them from rodeo.toml.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: Continue with Configuration and Running rodeo.
